text:
maria: ACME asked for something slightly different: not just demote-on-spike, but a predictable "safety net" that smooths short bursts while preserving reserved quota semantics. We need a spec and launch checklist.

sanjay: Agree. Key product goals: 1) preserve committed quota accounting, 2) accept short low-cost requests without failing, 3) make billing transparent. Suggest we call it `burst_safety_net` to avoid confusion with other pilots.

adele: Implementation idea: a per-tenant soft credit bucket that refills daily. Each tenant gets N safety credits (token-equivalent) that let short bursts bypass strict concurrency quota; when exhausted, normal quotas apply. Credits can be used only for requests under a token_limit and with latency under a short-window SLO.

adele: rough config example: ```yaml
burst_safety_net:
  enabled: true
  daily_credit_tokens: 250000
  per_request_token_limit: 1500
  max_burst_window_s: 15
  demotion_policy:
    - quantized_same_model
    - smaller_model
    - reject
  charge_behavior: bill_actual + credit_tracking
```

sanjay: Difference vs previous ideas: this preserves quota accounting (credits separate) and gives customers a predictable budget they can buy more of. Billing model: credits consumed are billed at a premium rate unless tenant purchases extra credits, where purchased credits have lower price. Need finance input.

billing-bot: billing: require event `burst_safetynet_use` with fields: tenant_id, tokens_used, orig_model, used_model, credit_consumed, billed_rate. Also support `burst_safetynet_purchase` for bought credits. Nightly reconcile must attach credits to invoices and apply premium/discount logic.

maria: Ops concerns: safety net must be pool-local and not create cross-tenant pressure. If many tenants use safety credits at once, we need a pool-level limiter and a contagion backoff that pauses credit draws when pool CPU/GPU pressure spikes.

adele: Runtime sketch: when request arrives, estimate tokens. If tokens <= per_request_token_limit and tenant has credits > 0 and pool pressure < threshold, accept request into an elastic slot. Elastic slot runs quantized variant if worker memory allows; otherwise route to prewarmed quantized worker in same pool. Deduct credits only after request completes (atomically). If credits exhausted mid-window, revert to quota enforcement.

sanjay: Also add a fast-fallback: if elastic slot can't be served within 200ms scheduling time, immediately demote to smaller_model routing to preserve latency SLO. That keeps p95 bounded.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Feature branch `burst_safety_net_v1` created; dry-run canary scheduled on prod-canary 2024-11-08T08:00Z.

maria: Ownership checklist draft: - API: tenant opt-in flag `burst_safety_net_v1` + purchase API for credits - Console: show credit balance, purchase path, daily consumption chart - Runtime: implement elastic slots, credit accounting, demotion chain, pool-level backoff - Telemetry: `burst_safetynet_use`, `burst_safetynet_credit_balance`, `burst_safetynet_blocked_due_to_pressure` - Ops: circuit breakers (pause credits at pool pressure), prewarm policy for quantized variants - Billing: events + purchase flow + nightly reconcile job - Legal: contract language for "safety net credits" and quality rollback clause - Pilot: ACME + 2 internal tenants for 14 days

billing-bot: finance: recommend letting purchased credits be refundable in pilot if QA shows regressions; need invoice sample and product messaging.

legal-anna: Draft contract blurb: "Burst Safety Net provides a limited number of daily credits that may allow short bursts to be served using lower-capacity model variants. Redwood will track credits consumed and bill accordingly. During pilot, customers may request refund of purchased credits tied to validated QA regressions as defined in the Pilot Acceptance."

adele: Launch acceptance criteria proposal: 1) Pilot length 14 days with ACME + 2 internal tenants, 2) Telemetry in place and nightly reconcile working, 3) p95 latency for safety-net accepted requests < 1.5x baseline, 4) pool-level contagion backoff tested with chaos test, 5) Billing events validated end-to-end and invoice sample provided, 6) Contract language approved, 7) Human-sample QA for demoted outputs with embedding-similarity thresholds defined.

sanjay: Fairness guard: per-tenant weekly cap on purchased credits without explicit approval, and pool-level throttling when aggregate safety_net consumption exceeds configurable percent of pool capacity (default 8%). If pool-level threshold crossed, new safety-net accepts return `429` with `safetynet_busy` code.

ops-bot: monitor-bot: adding alert `safetynet_pool_pressure` when safety_net_consumption > 8% of pool capacity for 10m or when demotion_rate > 1% and regional latency delta > 8% over 5m.

maria: UX note: display credit balance prominently and warn when projected daily usage will incur premium charges. Also add toggle to auto-purchase a small refill when balance < X tokens to avoid surprise rejections.

billing-bot: billing: ensure `purchase_refund_workflow` hook exists for pilot-era refunds. Finance will review.

sanjay: Risks & mitigations: - Contagion: mitigate with pool throttles + per-tenant caps - Quality regressions: require automated eval + sampled human review; rollback toggles per-tenant - Memory thrash: prefer routing to prewarmed quantized workers; include prewarm buffer in pool capacity - Billing surprise: show invoices in UI during pilot and offer refund path

adele: Implementation timeline suggestion: RFC this week, 1 sprint dev (runtime + billing stubs), 1 sprint for console + telemetry + ops runbook, pilot the week after for 2 weeks. If ACME agrees, we push into next sprint.

maria: Next steps: ADELE to write RFC with atomic credit accounting and scheduling flow. SANJAY to draft fairness caps and circuit settings. BILLING to prototype events and sample invoice. LEGAL to finalize pilot wording. Ops to prepare canary plan. Friday 3pm sync to finalize pilot runbook.

maria: Thanks team 680
